descriptionChirho: General adverb meaning 'well', 'rightly', or 'favorably', describing the manner in which something is done or the state of affairs. Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'bien' (well), Hindi 'भला' (bhalā = good/well) and 'अछ' (achh- = good), Arabic 'يَكونَ–لَكَ' (yakūna laka = may it be for you) and 'خَيْرًا' (khayran = good), Korean '잘' (jal = well), Swahili 'vizuri' (well/nicely) and 'vema' (well). This adverbial use describes quality or manner in general contexts, distinct from the exclamatory commendation sense.

Exclamatory adverb used as a formula of praise or commendation, meaning 'Well done!' or 'Good job!', typically addressed to a servant or faithful person. Multilingual evidence confirms the performative/exclamatory force: Spanish 'Bien' / 'Bien-hecho' (Well done), Hindi 'शाबाश' (shābāsh = bravo!, a dedicated exclamatory word), Arabic 'نِعِمَّا' (ni'immā = how excellent!) and 'أَحسَنتَ' (ahsanta = you did well!), Korean '잘하였다/잘했다' (jalhayeotda = you did well), Swahili 'Vema/Vizuri' (Well/Good). The Hindi 'शाबाश' is particularly diagnostic as it is solely an exclamation of praise.
